q: How do I calculate the emissions of supermarket display freezers and chillers?
title: Supermarket freezer electricity
short: Sub-meter the refrigerated cabinets, or take their share of the store bill, and multiply the kWh by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Add refrigerant top-ups from service invoices as Scope 1. A meter shows how open and doored cabinets compare in your store.
audience: Supermarket, grocery and convenience store operators

ul: Remote condensing units on the roof.
Night blinds or their absence on open cabinets.

p: Leaks from long pipe runs in remote systems can be large. Service invoices give the kilograms added, which go into Scope 1 at the gas's global warming potential.
Report refrigeration kWh per store and per square metre of sales floor, so stores of different sizes can be compared.

example.title: Worked example: one store's cabinets (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Total: 3,834 / 12 = 319.5 kg CO2 per cabinet a month
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use a sub-meter or the cabinet energy labels.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
